Subject: PO vs Card — follow-up and next steps (FinOpsCo)

Hi Samantha / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion and appreciate the transparency on your AP process. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Pilot: small-scale proof-of-concept (3 dev seats, ~100k tokens/month).
- Procurement preference: Finance prefers PO for enterprise purchases; procurement team handles vendor onboarding and requires W9/COI and signed SOW for vendor creation.
- For smaller pilot spend, the card is an option to speed up kick-off, but anything above $10k typically needs a PO and vendor onboarding.
- Marketplace interest: you asked whether Redwood is available via the Cloud Marketplace (yes — option to consolidate billing).

Proposed next steps:
1) I attached our Vendor Onboarding Packet and a draft SOW (Redwood_SOW_Draft_v1.pdf). Please share the packet with your procurement team and let me know if anything missing.
2) If you want to go the card route to start faster, confirm who will be the payment owner and whether a temporary limit is OK.
3) If you need PO / net30, please share the name/email of the person who will create/submit the PO and approximate timeline.
4) I can surface our SOC2 Type II report and any additional security artifacts — attaching a link for quick reference.

Action items for me:
- Send the vendor packet, SOW, and a DocuSign-ready SOW if you want to sign electronically.
- Share marketplace procurement link and billing flow for FinOpsCo.

If you prefer, we can do a short 15-min sync with procurement to walk through the vendor packet.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0127

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — super helpful. A few clarifications from procurement/finance side: 

- For pilots under $10k we typically allow a corporate card to avoid vendor onboarding delays. For anything expected to exceed that (or recurring monthly commitments), we require vendor creation and a PO.
- Vendor creation checklist we need: W9, COI, signed SOW or reseller agreement, vendor banking details (ACH).
- Our procurement lead (Tom Ellis) typically handles vendor ingestion — I’ve cc'd him here. Tom, would you be able to confirm the typical PO lead time once we have the packet?

Marketplace question: yes — if Redwood is listed in the Cloud Marketplace, we can route billing through there which reduces vendor onboarding friction and allows chargebacks per business unit. Would be good to see what billing options are supported there (monthly invoicing vs charge-to-project).

We can do the short 15-min sync. Tom, would 11:00am PT on Monday work for a quick call?

Best,
Samantha
Senior Procurement Manager | FinOpsCo
samantha.lee@finopsco.com

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Appreciate the clarifications. Quick answers and next items from our side: 

1) Vendor packet items — included in the attached PDF: W9, sample COI, vendor banking template, and instructions for ACH. If Tom needs the documents in a different format (e.g., supplier portal CSV), we can export.
2) Marketplace — Redwood is available on the Cloud Marketplace. I’m attaching a short note with the marketplace link and billing options. Marketplace billing supports monthly invoicing and charge-to-project via the marketplace billing account; however, the marketplace path can sometimes add a 3–5 day reprovisioning step depending on your entitlement flows.
3) PO timeline — Tom, typical vendor creation on our customers' side ranges 3–10 business days once packet + signed SOW are submitted. If you need an internal routing code or billing address to populate the PO, here are the details you asked for: 
   - Company name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
   - Billing address: 88 2nd St, Suite 200, San Francisco, CA 94105
   - Tax ID: 94-1234567
   - Invoices: invoices@redwood.ai

4) Pilot / Card option — if you want to start immediately by card, we can provision a temporary dev key and cap usage to the expected pilot spend. If you prefer PO from day one, we'll queue setup as soon as vendor creation + PO are filed.

Action items:
- I’ll send a DocuSign-ready SOW if you want to sign today (link included).
- Lauren (cc) from our Finance/Revenue Ops is on the thread if you need invoice or payment-terms confirmation.

Would love a quick confirmation on whether you prefer card-first or PO-first so we can prioritize.

Thanks —
